q.t: A force is a…
q.e: It results from two objects interacting.

q.t: The SI unit of force is the…
q.e: Named after Isaac Newton.

q.t: How many objects must interact for a force to exist?
q.e: At least two — each feels a force from the other.

q.t: The force that slows a rolling ball is…
q.e: It acts opposite to motion.

q.t: Friction acts…
o: Opposite to the direction of motion
q.e: That's why it slows things down.

q.t: Which is a non-contact force?
q.e: Magnetic and electrostatic forces are non-contact too.

q.t: Weight is…
o: The force with which Earth pulls an object
q.e: Its SI unit is the newton.

q.t: Mass is measured in…
q.e: Mass is the amount of matter.

q.t: The upward force of a liquid on an object is…
q.e: All liquids exert it.

q.t: Like charges…
q.e: Unlike charges attract.

q.t: A ball rolling on the ground stops on its own. This proves…
q.e: Whenever speed changes, a force must be acting.

q.t: A book rests on a table. Forces on it are…
q.e: At rest means forces balance, not absence of force.

q.t: Why is friction greater on rough surfaces?
q.e: Even smooth surfaces have tiny bumps.

q.t: Why are aeroplanes and trains streamlined?
q.e: Friction acts in gases and liquids too.

q.t: Gravitational force is…
q.e: Unlike magnetic and electrostatic forces.

q.t: A rubbed balloon and the woollen cloth that rubbed it…
q.e: They get opposite charges.

q.t: Two balloons rubbed with the same cloth…
q.e: Both get the same kind of charge.

q.t: A 1 kg object weighs about how many newtons on Earth?
q.e: About 10 N.

q.t: The same 1 kg object on the Moon has mass…
q.e: Mass doesn't change with place; weight does (1.6 N).

q.t: An object floats when…
q.e: If gravity is greater, it sinks.

q.t: A spring balance has 5 divisions between 0 N and 1 N. Least count (N)?
A spring balance has 10 divisions between two marks 2 N apart. Least count (N)?
Why is slipping easier on a wet floor?
q.e: Surfaces can no longer lock together.

q.t: Why is pedalling uphill harder?
o: You work against gravity pulling you down the slope
q.e: Plus friction.

q.t: At the top of a vertical throw, a ball…
q.e: Its motion reverses there.

q.t: Why does a mug feel lighter in water?
q.e: Upthrust pushes up.

q.t: Archimedes' principle: the buoyant force equals…
q.e: If displaced weight is less than the object's weight, it sinks.

q.t: Why does pumice float?
o: Trapped gas bubbles make it less dense than water
q.e: Lava cooled quickly, trapping bubbles.

q.t: Rubbed plastic picks up paper bits. This is…
q.e: A charged object attracts uncharged ones.

q.t: Ring magnets with like poles facing: the upper one…
q.e: Repulsion holds it up without contact.

q.t: A 5 kg bag weighs about how many newtons on Earth (1 kg ≈ 10 N)?
A 1 kg mass weighs 1.6 N on the Moon. What would a 10 kg mass weigh there (N)?
On which body does 1 kg weigh the most (from the table)?
q.e: Stronger gravity → more weight; mass stays 1 kg.

q.t: 'The weight of the wheat bag is 10 kg' is scientifically…
o: Wrong — kg is a unit of mass
q.e: In science use mass in kg, weight in N.

q.t: Which shows a force changing direction?
o: A bat hitting a moving ball
q.e: The ball's direction changes.

q.t: Which shows a force changing shape?
q.e: Force can change shape.

q.t: Static electricity and current electricity are…
o: The same charges — static at rest, current when moving
q.e: Moving charges are an electric current.

q.t: Muscular force inside the body helps…
q.e: Also pushes food along the alimentary canal.

q.t: Never hang an object heavier than a spring balance's maximum because…
q.e: Check the range first.

q.t: Why does a bicycle speed up downhill without pedalling?
o: Gravity pulls it down the slope
q.e: Gravity does the work.
